text: Given a UISP instance with 3 sites (2 site, 1 endpoint), when uisp_list_sites is called with no filter, then all 3 are returned; when called with site_type="endpoint", then only the 1 endpoint site is returned
Given a known site_id, when uisp_get_site is called, then it returns that site's name, type, status, and suspended flag
Given a site_id the upstream API does not recognize, when uisp_get_site is called, then it returns a structured not_found error, not an unhandled exception
Given a site_id with 2 devices and another site with 1 device, when uisp_list_devices is called with that site_id, then exactly the 2 devices for that site are returned
Given devices across two sites, when uisp_list_devices is called with no site_id, then devices from both sites are returned
Given devices of mixed role (ap, router), when uisp_list_devices is called with role="router", then only router devices are returned
Given a known device_id, when uisp_get_device is called, then it returns identification fields plus overview fields (status, uptime, cpu, outageScore)
Given a device_id the upstream API does not recognize, when uisp_get_device is called, then it returns a structured not_found error
Given outages of type outage and unreachable, one ongoing=true and one ongoing=false, when uisp_list_outages is called with in_progress=true, then only the ongoing one is returned
Given outages for two different devices, when uisp_list_outages is called with a device_id filter, then only that device's outages are returned
Given log entries of mixed level (info, warning, error), when uisp_list_logs is called with level="error", then only error-level entries are returned
Given log entries across two sites, when uisp_list_logs is called with a site_id filter, then only that site's entries are returned

Given 250 outages exist upstream (upstream page size 100) and max_items defaults to 200, when uisp_list_outages is called, then scanned equals 200, truncated is true, and the tool does not error or hang
Given 150 log entries exist upstream and max_items defaults to 200, when uisp_list_logs is called, then all 150 are returned, scanned equals 150, and truncated is false
Given a request to any tool with X-Uisp-Api-Key or X-Uisp-Base-Url missing, when the tool is called, then it returns the not_configured error envelope, not a raw exception
Given the upstream UISP instance returns 401 for a bad token, when any tool is called, then it returns the unauthorized structured error, not a stack trace
Given the upstream UISP instance is unreachable (connection/timeout error), when any tool is called, then it returns the upstream_error structured error
Given a site_id with zero devices, when uisp_list_devices is called, then it returns an empty devices list with a normal success response, not an error

Given two concurrent calls using two different X-Uisp-Api-Key/X-Uisp-Base-Url pairs pointing at two different UISP instances, when both run concurrently against uisp_list_sites, then each caller's result only contains its own instance's sites, verified at the header/credential level
Given the server's tools/list response, when inspected, then all 6 tools have readOnlyHint true and no tool name implies a write/delete/restart/config action

Review round 1 must-fix #1 regression: every tool function must close its UispClient (via client_factory()) after use, so the real httpx.AsyncClient is released instead of leaking per-call connections.
Review round 1 must-fix #1 regression, against the real UispClient (not the stub): a 2-page paginate_all call must reuse exactly one httpx.AsyncClient instance, not open a new one per upstream page.
evidence: pytest -q -> 31 passed (incl. this test), 2026-11-03, dev03; also exercised live via scratch/PRD-21265/smoke.py against a real ASGI app (uisp_list_logs through an unreachable host returned a single structured upstream_error with no connection-leak exceptions)

text: Review round 1 must-fix #2 regression: the worst-case total call duration (every retry at full timeout, every backoff hitting the Retry-After cap) must provably stay under the SOP's 120s hard cap.
evidence: pytest -q -> 31 passed (incl. this test); computed worst_case_total = 3*(5.0+20.0) + 2*5.0 = 85.0s < 120.0s, 2026-11-03, dev03
